A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same accountability-modeling study. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.2, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DST experiments on MultiWOZ and Snips, threshold and loss-weight ablations, and a GPT-4o mini user-simulator experiment (Tables 2–7).

after.justification: v2 retains original DST experiments, ablations, and user-simulator results, including the validation analysis in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The accountability head, joint training objective, and correction procedure in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. AMD, SC, and UC rename existing components. The corrected user-confirmation description agrees with Algorithm 1 and the prompts already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MultiWOZ 2.4 and Snips coverage and the same MultiWOZ user-simulator scenario. Removing two illustrative Snips cases does not remove Snips from the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a 12-system comparison in Table 3, including GPT-4o, IC-DST, OrchestraLLM, CorrectionLM, TripPy-R, and LDST. Oracle rows disappear from the main DST and user-simulator tables; the latter instead includes uncorrected AMD. Oracle correction remains a comparator in Figure 3.

E3.justification: ROC-AUC is removed from the evaluation metrics and Table 2. Data splits, backbone sizes, four-epoch training, validation-based selection, and correction thresholds remain unchanged. The new comparison table distinguishes zero-shot, few-shot, and supervised settings and labels LDST's 10% training-data condition.

E4.justification: The threshold analysis is reduced from v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 4, omitting several sweep rows, Slot-F1, and detailed oracle results. Two Snips case studies are removed. The loss-weight ablations, five MultiWOZ cases, and Llama oracle-headroom curve remain.

E5.justification: Both Appendix A.2 passages state that belief states are generated using a single run. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Table 3 adds prior-system results, including TripPy-R at 69.87 JGA alongside the retained 70.51 for AMD+SC. ROC-AUC results and many oracle and threshold entries are removed. Matched primary DST, user-simulator, and loss-weight results remain unchanged. The stated best Snips improvement changes from 2.5% to 1.5% relative, using unchanged underlying scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs, or derivations. The new error-rate description clarifies existing empirical metrics.

C1.justification: v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion newly claim state-of-the-art DST performance, extending v1's claim of improvement over backbone models. User-confirmation performance is promoted to an explicit main contribution, while the abstract describes reduced overreliance as a potential benefit. These changes use existing primary results.

C2.justification: v2 explains dataset-specific FPR/FNR behavior through JGA-based threshold selection, correcting v1's overbroad error-reduction account. It removes the hidden-size explanation for Gemma's performance, newly characterizes value errors as a minor concern, and qualifies the state-of-the-art comparison by excluding synthetic-data-trained systems. Section 8's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies that FPR and FNR measure percentages of turns containing the corresponding errors. Training hyperparameters, hardware, trainable-parameter counts, batch sizes, training times, appendix prompts, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands comparative positioning through the prior-system table and state-of-the-art claim. It adds references on correction, orchestration, function-calling DST, and positive friction, explains its baseline's relationship to LDST, and discusses excluding STAR and ASSIST because of additional synthetic training data.

P1.justification: The title gains 'Know Your Mistakes,' and the introduction and results narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Model terminology changes throughout. Qualitative analysis moves from Section 6.1 to 5.4, and user-overreliance discussion becomes standalone Section 6. These changes substantially reorganize the presentation of largely retained research.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to show both self-correction and user confirmation. A baseline table is added, Table 2 is restructured with relative-gain highlighting, and threshold and case-study tables are shortened. Figure 3 is relabeled and relocated with unchanged curves; appendix prompts are consolidated onto one page.

improvement.justification: The new prior-system comparison addresses v1's lack of explicit benchmark context, while the revised overview and corrected error-rate and confirmation explanations improve clarity and accuracy. These provide a limited net improvement with unchanged primary results. The gains are tempered by removal of ROC-AUC and detailed oracle evidence, and stronger real-world overreliance interpretations still rest on the same simulator study.
